name: Declared repeated cross sections
description: rcs option declares repeated cross sections when the data carry an identifier
notes: rcs is the counterpart of R did panel=FALSE: ivar() may be supplied alongside it, is validated and marks the estimation sample, then does not enter estimation, matching R which overwrites idname with a row sequence. Fixture is a balanced panel with a real identifier so both readings are well formed; the generator refuses to write it unless the two readings differ, and the test pins csdid to panel=FALSE and away from panel=TRUE. Verified on Stata 17 MP against R did 2.5.1: max |ATT| gap 6.7e-16, max |SE| gap 1.4e-17. Conflicting panel-shaped options bal(full), bal(pair) and fixweights(base|first) are refused with r(198).

name: Results export via saving()
description: saving() on every estat subcommand writes the result it computed
notes: Owner-directed: saving() is the Stata idiom for writing a result to a file, so it is an option on the subcommand rather than a separate export command. Before this it worked on estat tidy and estat glance only; estat attgt refused it and the five aggregation subcommands PARSED it and then ignored it, so estat event, saving(f) returned rc 0 and wrote no file. estat tidy and estat glance keep working and are undocumented, and the test pins them against the new spellings so the two paths cannot drift. Test qualified: seeding the aggregation branch back to ignoring saving() turns it red.

name: Pair-balanced 2x2
description: bal(pair) keeps the units observed in both periods of each 2x2
notes: Restores the per-comparison balancing Version 1.82 did silently. Verified against an independently derived oracle -- a two-period DiD per cell with the influence function built by hand, not did::att_gt, which has no such mode: max |ATT| gap 1.1e-16, max |SE| gap 3.5e-18, per-cell unit counts exact. The n_units/cell-count IF scaling could not be settled by reading the kernel and is settled by that oracle. e(panel_mode) reports pair-balanced, a fourth value: reporting allow_unbalanced would name a different estimator. The fast kernel is excluded because it assumes one fixed unit set per cell -- it produced the right ATT but reported unrestricted group sizes. Test qualified: disabling the per-cell mask turns it red.
